mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 1.0% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 1.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and a decline in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month window signals a shift from cyclical to structural supply constraints, which elevates inflationary pressures and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0% qoq and HOUST < 0% qoq for 3 months
regime_hint: transition from expansion to supply-constrained regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO rises and HOUST falls concurrently for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% during a recession signals a policy-driven liquidity injection, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages signals robust demand growth, which lifts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and a deceleration in housing starts (HOUST) over a 6-month window indicates a shift toward manufacturing-led growth and away from housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to capital expenditure cycles.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 0% qoq for 6 months AND HOUST < 0% qoq for 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO accelerates and HOUST decelerates for six months.
